title: A fallback declaration is dropped before a relative color that cannot be resolved, even for targets without relative color syntax
impact: No reactions, agent-style batch report, and the reporter's exact value (`lch(from currentColor l c h)`) is a no-op nobody writes. But the same bug hits a plausible pattern: a fallback before a translucent currentColor, e.g. `color:#0003;color:color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 20%, transparent)` or `rgb(from currentColor r g b / 20%)`, with targets older than Chrome 111/Safari 16.2 (color-mix) or Chrome 119/Safari 16.4 (relative colors). Those browsers then inherit instead of using the fallback, silently. The window of affected targets is shrinking.
code: src/properties/prefix_handler.rs: FallbackHandler, Property::Unparsed arm ("Unparsed properties are always valid", replaces dest[index])
summary: For properties handled by FallbackHandler (color, fill, stroke, caret-color, caret, text-shadow, filter, backdrop-filter), an Unparsed value always replaces the earlier declaration. That's right when the value has var()/env() (a browser accepts it at parse time, so the fallback could never apply), but wrong when lightningcss keeps the value as tokens because it can't resolve it (currentColor origin, color-mix with currentColor): old browsers reject that declaration at parse time and would have used the fallback. border-color, background-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color and background-image already keep the fallback.
repro: 1392-repro.mjs. Chrome 100 targets: `.a{color:#0003;color:color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 20%, transparent)}` -> `.a{color:color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 20%, transparent)}` (fallback dropped); same for `rgb(from currentColor r g b / 20%)`, fill, text-shadow. Controls (correct today): border-color keeps both; var() origin drops the fallback (correct, see evidence); Chrome 130 drops it (correct); `lch(from red l c h)` is resolved.
evidence: scripts/repro.mjs on local (master), 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1: same output; releases <= ~1.25 panic on currentColor in fallbacks (fixed earlier), so not a regression. Browser check in Chromium with an unsupported function as stand-in for a pre-119 browser: `color:blue;color:fake-rcs(from var(--c) l c h)` computes to the inherited color (fallback useless, IACVT), while `color:blue;color:fake-rcs(from currentColor l c h)` computes to blue. So the fallback matters exactly for the non-var() case. Checked properties via the JS API with Chrome 100 targets. Workaround verified: `.a{color:blue} @supports (color: rgb(from red r g b)){.a{color:lch(from currentColor l c h)}}` with Chrome 100 targets keeps both rules.

fix.approach: In FallbackHandler's Unparsed arm, when browser targets are set and the token list has no var()/env() (i.e. it's unparsed because it couldn't be resolved, not because of substitution), keep the earlier declaration and push the new one, mirroring the parsed branch's `!is_compatible(targets)` path. Optionally narrow to token lists whose color functions aren't supported by the targets. Add tests in lib.rs next to the relative color/color-mix tests, for color and text-shadow.

draftReply:
Thanks, confirmed on master and 1.33.0. With targets older than relative color support, `color: blue` is removed before a value we can't resolve at build time (like `lch(from currentColor l c h)`), so older browsers lose the fallback. The same happens with `color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 20%, transparent)` for targets without `color-mix()`, and affects `color`, `fill`, `stroke`, `caret-color`, `text-shadow` and `filter`; `border-color` and `background-color` already keep the fallback.

When the value contains `var()`, removing the fallback is correct: a browser accepts the declaration at parse time, so the fallback could never apply there.

Until it's fixed, a workaround is to put the newer value in `@supports (color: rgb(from red r g b)) { ... }`.
